reply.text:
Electrolytes can help in specific situations, like long sweaty sessions in the heat or runs past an hour or so, but for most training and a normal diet, water and regular food cover it. I can't give you an amount of sodium, since that depends on your sweat, your diet and your health, so check with a doctor or a dietitian for what's right for you. If you have a blood pressure or kidney concern, that conversation matters even more.

If you tell me what kind of sessions you're thinking of, I can talk through hydration around them in general terms.
